aligned.evidence: components/status/StatusPill.jsx STATUS map (each entry has ink/surface/line + glyph + label, plus pulse/beacon); tokens/status.css header lists the 4 channels; CLAUDE_DESIGN_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md L1051 'Do not rely only on color for state'

aligned.point: Glyph vocabulary is distinct per status and rendered in mono so markers align in dense rows, and critical adds a hazard hatch so it reads in grayscale — matching readme §4 'geometric Unicode markers ... always paired with a label' and the RiskBadge critical-hatch requirement.
aligned.evidence: tokens/status.css --glyph-* tokens + .cp-hazard repeating-linear-gradient; components/status/RiskBadge.jsx isCritical => className 'cp-hazard'

gaps.gap: Session status vocabulary is drastically undersized. The kit only ever uses 7 session status strings (active, running, waiting-human, waiting-perm, failed, completed, conflict) against the canonical 17-state Session machine. Missing entirely: creating, starting, thinking, running_command, editing_files, running_tests, waiting_on_external_service, idle, stale, changes_ready, archived, killed. StatusPill has 'editing'/'testing' keys but they are never used in data and do not map to canonical names; 'conflict' is applied to sessions though it is not a Session state.
gaps.kit_evidence: kit-data.js sessions[].status (only waiting-human/running/active/failed/completed used); StatusPill.jsx STATUS keys lack thinking/running_command/running_tests/changes_ready/creating/starting/idle/stale/killed/waiting_on_external_service; kit-data status enumeration shows 14 distinct strings total across ALL objects
gaps.doc_ref: ARCHITECTURE.md §5.1 Session(17, R-4); PRD §10 SESS-3; UX §8.1
gaps.recommendation: Change the kit (build target): define the canonical 17 Session states as the StatusPill status vocabulary, mapping each to a (color, glyph, label, attention-level) tuple; rename hyphenated keys to the canonical snake_case enum at the data layer.
gaps.for_tasks_gen: tasks-gen MUST require a Session StatusPill that renders all 17 canonical states (creating, starting, active, thinking, running_command, editing_files, running_tests, waiting_on_permission, waiting_on_human_input, waiting_on_external_service, idle, stale, changes_ready, failed, completed, archived, killed) each with a distinct glyph+label+attention-rank, and a frontend component test asserting one rendering per state (§14 frontend tier).

Likewise 'waiting-perm' vs canonical 'waiting_on_permission'. The kit's casual hyphenated tokens are not the binding enum and will not round-trip to projection status values.

gaps.gap: The Attention Ladder is hard-capped at 4 mapped states and silently floors everything else to 0. The sidebar maps only {waiting-human:5, failed:4, running:2, active:1} and 'Needs my attention' filters only ['waiting-human','failed']. So stale, blocked, conflict, waiting-permission, degraded, high-context, changes_ready, idle never receive their PRD/UX attention rank — e.g. a permission-waiting or conflicted session would sort as rank 0 (idle) and never appear in 'Needs my attention'.
gaps.kit_evidence: kit-shell.jsx L183 inline map {'waiting-human':5,failed:4,running:2,active:1}||0; kit-views.jsx L26 attention=filter(['waiting-human','failed'])
gaps.doc_ref: ARCHITECTURE.md §5.1; PRD §5.2 (7-rank order incl. permission requested, failed/stale/conflicted, changes ready); UX §5.1 / CLAUDE_DESIGN_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md §1 attention-first hierarchy
gaps.recommendation: Change the kit: replace the inline 4-entry map with a single canonical status->attention-rank table covering every §5.1 state, and derive both the 'Needs my attention' membership and sort order from it (waiting_on_permission, conflict, blocked, stale, failing-checks must rank into attention).
gaps.for_tasks_gen: tasks-gen MUST require ONE canonical status->attention-rank mapping table (covering all 9 machines' relevant states) as the single source for sidebar weight, queue membership, and sort order; specify the PRD §5.2 ordering (waiting_on_human_input > waiting_on_permission > failed/stale/conflicted > active/running_tests > changes_ready > idle > completed/archived) and a test asserting permission/conflict/stale sessions surface in 'Needs my attention'.

gaps.gap: No Approval-vs-ActionRequest split. The architecture defines TWO state machines (Approval: requested..approved/denied/edited/auto_approved_by_policy/expired/cancelled/escalated; and ActionRequest/execution: submitted..policy_decided..queued/executing/succeeded/failed/partially_succeeded/rolled_back/rollback_failed). The kit collapses both into a single approve/deny gesture and a flat StatusPill set, with no executing/partially_succeeded/rolled_back/policy_decided/escalated/expired states represented anywhere.
gaps.kit_evidence: kit-overlays.jsx L68-69 only Deny / Approve buttons; kit-tasks.jsx onResolve(item,'Approved'|'Denied'); StatusPill.jsx has 'approved' but no submitted/policy_decided/queued/executing/partially_succeeded/rolled_back/rollback_failed/edited/auto_approved_by_policy/escalated/expired; UX §9 Screen 16 lists Executing/Partially succeeded/Failed-with-recovery states that are unrendered
gaps.doc_ref: ARCHITECTURE.md §0.3 R-5 + §5.1 Approval(10) & ActionRequest(15); UX §8.7 + Screen 16 'Important states' (Executing, Partially succeeded, Stale preconditions)
gaps.recommendation: Change the kit: model Approval status and ActionRequest/execution status as two distinct pills; render the Gateway modal lifecycle (preview pending/succeeded/unavailable -> awaiting_approval -> executing -> succeeded|failed|partially_succeeded|rolled_back) and the stale-precondition re-approval path.
gaps.for_tasks_gen: tasks-gen MUST require two separate status renderings (Approval machine + ActionRequest/execution machine per §5.1 R-5), the Action Gateway modal showing post-approval execution states (executing/partially_succeeded/rolled_back/rollback_failed) and the §6.2/§17 stale_precondition 'requires fresh approval' state; bind to R-5.

gaps.gap: Worktree status is reduced to 3 buckets with no derived-status precedence. The kit collapses worktree status to {dirty, active->'Clean', conflict} and an unrelated 'active' graph-node status, missing the canonical derived model: git-axis {clean,dirty,untracked_files,conflicts,behind_base,ahead_of_base} + lifecycle overlay {creating,locked,pr_open,merged,prunable,deleted} resolved by a precedence function (locked/conflicts > dirty > ahead/behind > clean).

gaps.doc_ref: ARCHITECTURE.md §0.3 R-7 + §5.1 Worktree(derived) + §7.2 (precedence fn, re-read git2 live); UX §8.3 (11 worktree statuses)
gaps.recommendation: Change the kit: drive worktree status from the two-axis derived model and show the precedence-winning state (e.g. conflicts/locked beat dirty), and surface untracked/ahead/behind/pr_open/merged/prunable distinctly rather than one 'Clean'/'Dirty'/'Conflict' bucket.
gaps.for_tasks_gen: tasks-gen MUST require a Worktree status renderer driven by the derived git-axis x overlay precedence function (§7.2), surfacing all UX §8.3 states, plus a unit test for the precedence collapse (locked/conflicts > dirty > ahead/behind > clean).

gaps.gap: PR status is incoherent and undersized: kit-data uses a free-text 'lane' (open/ready/merged) plus a separate 'status' field that conflicts (e.g. a 'merged' lane PR carries status:'pr-open'), and only 3 lanes are rendered. The canonical PullRequest machine has 11 states (draft, open, checks_pending, checks_failing, needs_review, changes_requested, approved, mergeable, conflict, merged, closed), GitHub-authoritative with re-fetch-before-merge.

gaps.for_tasks_gen: tasks-gen MUST require a PullRequest StatusPill over the canonical 11 states and PR lanes mapped to those states (UX Screen 9), with the 'mergeable' gate reflecting a GitHub re-fetch (§7.2) before the Merge action is enabled.

gaps.gap: Time-derived 'stale' status (and the broader stale/degraded family) is defined in the kit (StatusPill 'stale','degraded'; ladder rank 3) but never produced on any session/profile/brain instance, and there is no notion of it being daemon-time-derived (recomputed on rebuild) vs event-derived. Stale sessions/profiles/brain are a PRD §5.5 risk surface the kit never shows.
